angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,597,740 km at 43.55 pc = 2.33 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93683: distance 43.554 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.01), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 43.554 +/- 0.436 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 23.8121 +/- 0.1518 mas (same row, RUWE 2.48), 156.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.921 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93683: radius 10.921 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 61.216 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.052) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,597,740 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4889 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93683: effective temperature 4889 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.046) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93683: effective temperature 4889 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.046) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * omi Sgr: spectral type G9IIIb (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * omi Sgr: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 255 (BS 7217)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.7 from 2014ApJ...785...94L; the 10 published values span log g 2.5 to 3.03, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...785...94L)
